clinician.trajectory_summary: An 82-year-old male presented with sudden onset seizures. Initial MRI showed multiple CNS lesions with peripheral contrast enhancement, suggestive of pyogenic or neoplastic nature (E001). Initial workup included positive serology for Entamoeba histolytica (E003) and CSF analysis showing increased proteins and lactate, but negative PCR/culture for common pathogens, T. gondii, Cryptococcus, and E. histolytica (E008). The patient was treated for presumed 'cerebral abscesses', but this treatment failed to improve his condition (E005). A total-body CT scan revealed bilateral bronchiectasis and a lung cavitation (E005), and bronchoalveolar lavage was negative for various pathogens including Mycobacterium tuberculosis, common bacteria/fungi, Pneumocystis jirovecii, and cytomegalovirus (E006). A biopsy of the CNS lesions was performed, which demonstrated histiocytic granulomatous tissue with a conspicuous plasmacellular component, defined as an IgG subtype 4 producer (ratio IgG4/IgG 45% on histological specimen, IgG4 > 10/HPF) (E009), confirming IgG4-related disease. Following this diagnosis, steroid treatment (prednisone 1 mg/Kg twice daily) was initiated, and antibiotic treatment was stopped. The patient showed significant clinical improvement within 10 days, becoming able to walk with minimal aid by the second week of treatment (E010).

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial MRI showed multiple CNS lesions with peripheral contrast enhancement, suggestive of pyogenic or neoplastic nature.
CSF analysis ruled out active CNS infection by common pathogens, T. gondii, Cryptococcus, and E. histolytica.
Bronchoalveolar lavage ruled out various pulmonary infections.
Histology of CNS lesions demonstrated histiocytic granulomatous tissue with a conspicuous plasmacellular component, defined as an IgG subtype 4 producer (ratio IgG4/IgG 45%, IgG4 > 10/HPF).
Clinical improvement was observed after initiation of steroid treatment and cessation of antibiotics.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Active CNS infection (bacterial, viral, fungal, parasitic)
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Negative CSF PCR/culture for common pathogens, T. gondii, Cryptococcus, and E. histolytica (E008); negative BAL for various pulmonary pathogens (E006); failure of antibiotic treatment (E005).

While initially suggested by MRI (E001), the CNS lesion biopsy revealed histiocytic granulomatous tissue with IgG4-producing plasma cells (E009), which is characteristic of IgG4-related disease rather than melanoma metastasis. Total-body CT did not explicitly mention metastatic lesions (E005).

remaining_uncertainties: Specific details of the antibiotic regimen administered for the presumed 'cerebral abscesses' and the precise clinical or imaging findings that indicated its failure.
Serum IgG4 levels were not reported.
Long-term clinical course or treatment response beyond the initial improvement.
